Title: The Cranberries :: Official Site - Biography
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
The tiny Flag Café was the venue on November 18th, 1989 as teenage Limerick four-piece The Cranberry Saw Us played their first hometown gig.
Bonding over a shared love of Joy Division, New Order, The Smiths and Talking Heads, the line-up that afternoon was Noel Hogan on guitar, his younger brother Mike on bass, Fergal Lawler on drums and Niall Quinn on vocals.
When Niall decided a few months later that his rock ‘n’ roll future lay elsewhere, he hooked Noel, Mike and Ferg up with a female singer who was in his girlfriend Catherine Hayes’ class at Laurel Hill school.
They weren’t sure what to make of Dolores O’Riordan when she arrived for her audition wearing a shiny pink tracksuit and with a Casio keyboard tucked under her arm – but knew they’d struck gold when she launched into a spinetingling version of ‘Nothing Compares 2 U’, which did Prince and Sinéad O’Connor proud.
As she left to go home, Noel handed Dolores a cassette containing a rough version of an instrumental they’d been working on, and asked her to have a go at finishing it off.
Within a few days she’d come up with the melodies and lyrics for ‘Linger’, a song which perfectly encapsulates the heartbreak of teenage love.
Dolores now officially on board, the newly abbreviated Cranberries started sending out demo tapes featuring ‘Linger’ and such other future classics as ‘Sunday’ and ‘Dreams’.
This triggered a frenzied industry bidding war which was won in 1991 by Island Records, already home to fellow Irish band U2, who promptly put Dolores, Noel, Mike and Ferg to work in the studio.
After the first few sessions failed to click, their legendary A&R man Denny Cordell asked the band to compile a producer wish-list.
Aiming high, Noel suggested Stephen Street and was shocked and delighted in equal measure when the Smiths and Blur go-to said “Yes!”
Recorded in Dublin and London, The Cranberries’ debut album, Everybody Else Is Doing It, So Why Can’t We?, was released on March 1st, 1993 with the cover featuring a shot of the band sat on a sofa, which soon became almost as famous as them!

It didn’t make much of an impact at first, but then ‘Linger’ exploded in the States where, thanks to the brilliant film noir video accompanying it, the band were embraced by the MTV generation.
The Cranberries’ next big thing status was confirmed when Michael Stipe turned up at the shoot and later invited Dolores and the boys to open for R.E.M.
“I was instantly captivated by The Cranberries,” Michael said in the band’s official Why Can’t We? book published by Ireland’s Hot Press magazine. “They were this young, vibrant, super-excited group of people who were making beautiful music. Dolores inherited the Irish storytelling tradition that’s been passed down from generation to generation. She just shone and you knew the band were going to be superstars.”
And so it turned out to be with Everybody Else… eventually climbing to no. 18 on the US Billboard 100 and selling 3.2 million copies in America alone.
Along with their own increasingly big gigs, The Cranberries also went out on an arena tour with Duran Duran whose posters had adorned Dolores’ bedroom walls growing up.
“We went from playing the Psychic Pig in Trowbridge to Radio City Music Hall in New York in the space of twelve months,” Noel Hogan says of their rapid ascent. “It was pure craziness.”
By the time their second album, No Need To Argue, was released on October 3rd, 1994, The Cranberries were an arena-headlining act in their own right with fans on all five continents.
Once again produced by Stephen Street, lead single ‘Zombie’ immediately entered the pantheon of great protest songs, Dolores bristling with righteous anger as she called out violent governments and terrorist organisations.
A number one record in Ireland, the UK, France, Germany, Austria. Spain, Sweden, New Zealand and Australia, No Need To Argue’s success lead to The Cranberries playing to 164,000 people at Woodstock ’94; George Clooney taking care of the introductions when they performed on Saturday Night Live; Dolores appearing on the cover of Rolling Stone; and her and Noel receiving a coveted Ivor Novello International Achievement Award.

“I really think that what makes people tune into The Cranberries is the honesty of the music,” Dolores noted at the time. “Some fans say, ‘Aren’t you embarrassed singing about such things?’ and I say, ‘That’s what makes me what I am.’ I’m not going to change for anyone.”
Dedicated to Denny Cordell and Dolores’ grandfather Joe Greensmith who’d both recently passed away, 1996’s To The Faithful Departed was produced by AC/DC, Bon Jovi and Van Halen man Bruce Fairbairn who brought his rock A-game with him.
Among its fifteen pulsating tracks was one of Dolores’ most personal songs yet, ‘When You’re Gone’ which included such heartrending couplets as: “Hold on to love, that is what I do/ Now that I've found you/ And from above, everything's stinking/ They're not around you.”
The extended version of the album included the spinetingling version of ‘Ava Maria’ she’d performed in September 1995 with Pavarotti as part of his Together For The Children Of Bosnia concert.
Afterwards, Simon Le Bon introduced Dolores O’Riordan to Princess Diana who professed to being a Cranberries fan.
There was more rubbing shoulders with royalty in 1998 when The Cranberries played at the Nobel Peace Prize ceremony attended by the King Of Norway.
Resplendent in a striking Storm Thorgerson cover, 1999’s Bury The Hatchet saw another change of producer with David Bowie, Radiohead and Depeche Mode man Ben Fenner adding his studio sheen to the likes of ‘Animal Instinct’, ‘Promises’ and ‘Just My Imagination’.
By now The Cranberries were etched into popular culture with Family Guy, Derry Girls, The Office US, Pitch Perfect, Clueless, Yellowjackets, Army Of The Dead, Roswell and New Mexico some of the major films and TV series they’ve helped to soundtrack.
Latterly, ‘Dreams’ has taken on a new life as the Limerick Gaelic football and hurling anthem while ‘Zombie’ blasts out of the P.A. whenever the Ireland rugby team play at home in Dublin's Aviva Stadium.

Stephen Street was back in the fold for 2001’s Wake Up And Smell The Coffee which was the sound of a band reinvigorated.
“Everyone was feeling good, nobody was burnt out and we were ready to go for it again with more confidence,” Fergal Lawler says of the album, which became an instant fan favourite. “And we worked with Stephen again – it was just what we needed, that passion he got out of us as players.”
A deeply spiritual person, Dolores was overjoyed when shortly after Wake Up And Smell The Coffee’s release she was invited to perform at the Concerto di Natale in The Vatican and granted an audience with Pope John Paul II.
She also got to sing for and meet his successor, Pope Francis, on a 2013 return trip to Rome.
After thirteen years on the writing/recording/touring treadmill, The Cranberries in September 2003 announced a two year hiatus, which ended up lasting until 2009.
During the break, Dolores released two well-received solo albums, Are You Listening? and No Baggage, while Noel recorded with a number of different people under the Mono Band banner, and Fergal also spent time in the studio producing albums by a number of Irish artists.
The catalyst for The Cranberries reuniting was Dolores being made an honorary patron of Trinity College Dublin’s Philosophical Society.
What no one knew until the night was that she’d invited Noel and Mike to perform an intimate acoustic session with her.
Given the musical magic which ensued, it was no surprise when afterwards the band announced that they were getting back together.
Released in 2012 and featuring the likes of ‘Fire And Soul’, ‘Raining In My Heart’ and ‘Conduct’, the Stephen Street-produced Roses album seamlessly picked up where The Cranberries had left off a decade earlier and earned them a whole new generation of fans.
Living up to its title, 2017’s Something Else found Dolores, Noel, Mike and Ferg back on their signature sofa and treating fans to ten orchestral and unplugged versions of previous hit singles – among them ‘Linger’, ‘Dreams’, ‘Zombie’ and ‘Ode To My Family’ – as well as serving up three stunning new tunes.

texts.0:
The tiny Flag Café was the venue on November 18th, 1989 as teenage Limerick four-piece The Cranberry Saw Us played their first hometown gig.
Bonding over a shared love of Joy Division, New Order, The Smiths and Talking Heads, the line-up that afternoon was Noel Hogan on guitar, his younger brother Mike on bass, Fergal Lawler on drums and Niall Quinn on vocals.
When Niall decided a few months later that his rock ‘n’ roll future lay elsewhere, he hooked Noel, Mike and Ferg up with a female singer who was in his girlfriend Catherine Hayes’ class at Laurel Hill school.
They weren’t sure what to make of Dolores O’Riordan when she arrived for her audition wearing a shiny pink tracksuit and with a Casio keyboard tucked under her arm – but knew they’d struck gold when she launched into a spinetingling version of ‘Nothing Compares 2 U’, which did Prince and Sinéad O’Connor proud.
As she left to go home, Noel handed Dolores a cassette containing a rough version of an instrumental they’d been working on, and asked her to have a go at finishing it off.
Within a few days she’d come up with the melodies and lyrics for ‘Linger’, a song which perfectly encapsulates the heartbreak of teenage love.
Dolores now officially on board, the newly abbreviated Cranberries started sending out demo tapes featuring ‘Linger’ and such other future classics as ‘Sunday’ and ‘Dreams’.
This triggered a frenzied industry bidding war which was won in 1991 by Island Records, already home to fellow Irish band U2, who promptly put Dolores, Noel, Mike and Ferg to work in the studio.
After the first few sessions failed to click, their legendary A&R man Denny Cordell asked the band to compile a producer wish-list.
Aiming high, Noel suggested Stephen Street and was shocked and delighted in equal measure when the Smiths and Blur go-to said “Yes!”
Recorded in Dublin and London, The Cranberries’ debut album, Everybody Else Is Doing It, So Why Can’t We?, was released on March 1st, 1993 with the cover featuring a shot of the band sat on a sofa, which soon became almost as famous as them!
texts.1:
It didn’t make much of an impact at first, but then ‘Linger’ exploded in the States where, thanks to the brilliant film noir video accompanying it, the band were embraced by the MTV generation.
The Cranberries’ next big thing status was confirmed when Michael Stipe turned up at the shoot and later invited Dolores and the boys to open for R.E.M.
“I was instantly captivated by The Cranberries,” Michael said in the band’s official Why Can’t We? book published by Ireland’s Hot Press magazine. “They were this young, vibrant, super-excited group of people who were making beautiful music. Dolores inherited the Irish storytelling tradition that’s been passed down from generation to generation. She just shone and you knew the band were going to be superstars.”
And so it turned out to be with Everybody Else… eventually climbing to no. 18 on the US Billboard 100 and selling 3.2 million copies in America alone.
Along with their own increasingly big gigs, The Cranberries also went out on an arena tour with Duran Duran whose posters had adorned Dolores’ bedroom walls growing up.
“We went from playing the Psychic Pig in Trowbridge to Radio City Music Hall in New York in the space of twelve months,” Noel Hogan says of their rapid ascent. “It was pure craziness.”
By the time their second album, No Need To Argue, was released on October 3rd, 1994, The Cranberries were an arena-headlining act in their own right with fans on all five continents.
Once again produced by Stephen Street, lead single ‘Zombie’ immediately entered the pantheon of great protest songs, Dolores bristling with righteous anger as she called out violent governments and terrorist organisations.
A number one record in Ireland, the UK, France, Germany, Austria. Spain, Sweden, New Zealand and Australia, No Need To Argue’s success lead to The Cranberries playing to 164,000 people at Woodstock ’94; George Clooney taking care of the introductions when they performed on Saturday Night Live; Dolores appearing on the cover of Rolling Stone; and her and Noel receiving a coveted Ivor Novello International Achievement Award.
texts.2:
“I really think that what makes people tune into The Cranberries is the honesty of the music,” Dolores noted at the time. “Some fans say, ‘Aren’t you embarrassed singing about such things?’ and I say, ‘That’s what makes me what I am.’ I’m not going to change for anyone.”
Dedicated to Denny Cordell and Dolores’ grandfather Joe Greensmith who’d both recently passed away, 1996’s To The Faithful Departed was produced by AC/DC, Bon Jovi and Van Halen man Bruce Fairbairn who brought his rock A-game with him.
Among its fifteen pulsating tracks was one of Dolores’ most personal songs yet, ‘When You’re Gone’ which included such heartrending couplets as: “Hold on to love, that is what I do/ Now that I've found you/ And from above, everything's stinking/ They're not around you.”
The extended version of the album included the spinetingling version of ‘Ava Maria’ she’d performed in September 1995 with Pavarotti as part of his Together For The Children Of Bosnia concert.
Afterwards, Simon Le Bon introduced Dolores O’Riordan to Princess Diana who professed to being a Cranberries fan.
There was more rubbing shoulders with royalty in 1998 when The Cranberries played at the Nobel Peace Prize ceremony attended by the King Of Norway.
Resplendent in a striking Storm Thorgerson cover, 1999’s Bury The Hatchet saw another change of producer with David Bowie, Radiohead and Depeche Mode man Ben Fenner adding his studio sheen to the likes of ‘Animal Instinct’, ‘Promises’ and ‘Just My Imagination’.
By now The Cranberries were etched into popular culture with Family Guy, Derry Girls, The Office US, Pitch Perfect, Clueless, Yellowjackets, Army Of The Dead, Roswell and New Mexico some of the major films and TV series they’ve helped to soundtrack.
Latterly, ‘Dreams’ has taken on a new life as the Limerick Gaelic football and hurling anthem while ‘Zombie’ blasts out of the P.A. whenever the Ireland rugby team play at home in Dublin's Aviva Stadium.
texts.3:
Stephen Street was back in the fold for 2001’s Wake Up And Smell The Coffee which was the sound of a band reinvigorated.
“Everyone was feeling good, nobody was burnt out and we were ready to go for it again with more confidence,” Fergal Lawler says of the album, which became an instant fan favourite. “And we worked with Stephen again – it was just what we needed, that passion he got out of us as players.”
A deeply spiritual person, Dolores was overjoyed when shortly after Wake Up And Smell The Coffee’s release she was invited to perform at the Concerto di Natale in The Vatican and granted an audience with Pope John Paul II.
She also got to sing for and meet his successor, Pope Francis, on a 2013 return trip to Rome.
After thirteen years on the writing/recording/touring treadmill, The Cranberries in September 2003 announced a two year hiatus, which ended up lasting until 2009.
During the break, Dolores released two well-received solo albums, Are You Listening? and No Baggage, while Noel recorded with a number of different people under the Mono Band banner, and Fergal also spent time in the studio producing albums by a number of Irish artists.
The catalyst for The Cranberries reuniting was Dolores being made an honorary patron of Trinity College Dublin’s Philosophical Society.
What no one knew until the night was that she’d invited Noel and Mike to perform an intimate acoustic session with her.
Given the musical magic which ensued, it was no surprise when afterwards the band announced that they were getting back together.
Released in 2012 and featuring the likes of ‘Fire And Soul’, ‘Raining In My Heart’ and ‘Conduct’, the Stephen Street-produced Roses album seamlessly picked up where The Cranberries had left off a decade earlier and earned them a whole new generation of fans.
Living up to its title, 2017’s Something Else found Dolores, Noel, Mike and Ferg back on their signature sofa and treating fans to ten orchestral and unplugged versions of previous hit singles – among them ‘Linger’, ‘Dreams’, ‘Zombie’ and ‘Ode To My Family’ – as well as serving up three stunning new tunes.

The 41st Ivors were presented on May 30, 1996, at the Grosvenor House, London.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ivor_Novello_Award_winners_and_nominees_(1990s%E2%80%932000s)#cite_note-7)

Title: Nominations announced for The Ivors 2022
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
This year’s nominees have been revealed, celebrating outstanding songwriters and composers.
We have announced the nominations for The Ivors with Apple Music 2022 for outstanding songwriting and composing across nine categories – including **Songwriter of the Year**, **Best Contemporary Song**, **Best Original Scores for Film, Television and Video Games**, and the **Rising Star Award with Apple Music**.
Recognised as a pinnacle of creative musical achievement since they were first presented in 1956, winning an Ivor Novello Award holds a special place in music as they are judged by award-winning songwriters and composers from The Ivors Academy.
This year’s list of nominations celebrates 77 individual songwriters and composers, including Adele – who is in the running for two awards – and Ed Sheeran, who is nominated for three Ivors. Up for four awards, Dean ‘Inflo’ Josiah Cover is this year’s most nominated songwriter. He is recognised for his work with fellow nominees Cleo Soul and Little Simz, who has also received two nominations.
**Shaznay Lewis, Ivor Novello Award winner and judge for The Ivors**, said: _“It’s been a standout year for music and I am full of admiration for the 77 talented songwriters and composers we are celebrating this year. Their work and words touch on a dizzying range of emotions, and I count myself lucky to have heard their stories. As it has every year since 1956, The Ivors celebrates the outstanding creation of music, and I’d like to say a huge congratulations to every nominee.”_
This year sees five huge artists in the running for **Songwriter of the Year**. The prestigious award recognises songwriters or songwriting partnerships for outstanding bodies of songs released in 2021, with Adele, Coldplay, Dave, Ed Sheeran, and Raye up for the award this year. For the second year, members of The Ivors Academy will vote for the winner.

Celebrating albums released in the UK in 2021 that exhibit creative consistency and exceptional songwriting, this year’s nominees for **Best Album** include Laura Mvula’s ‘Pink Noise’ – co-written with Dann Hume, and Sleaford Mods for ‘Spare Ribs’. Receiving three of his four nominations in this category is Dean ‘Inflo’ Josiah Cover for his work with Cleo Sol on both her album ‘Mother’ and SAULT’s ‘NINE’ alongside fellow co-writer Jack Peñate, and with Little Simz for ‘Sometimes I Might Be Introvert’.
Celebrating excellence in the craft of songwriting, this year’s **Best Song Musically and Lyrically** consists of a star-studded line up with nominations for Rag’n’Bone Man’s ‘All You Ever Wanted’, Adele’s emotional hit ‘Easy On Me’, Ella Henderson’s ‘Let’s Go Home Together’, Sam Fender’s ‘Seventeen Going Under’ and Holly Humberstone’s ‘Haunted House’, with their co-writers.
This year’s category for **Best Contemporary Song** also features Rising Star Award nominee PinkPantheress for ‘Just For Me’, as well as a second nominations Little Simz for ‘I Love You, I Hate You’. Also recognised for outstanding originality in songwriting are Russ Millions and Tion Wayne for ‘Body’, James Blake and SZA for ‘Coming Back’, and FKA twigs, Headie One and Fred again.. for ‘Don’t Judge Me’.
Now in its third year, the **Rising Star Award with Apple Music** discovers, supports and accelerates the careers of the most promising young UK or Irish songwriters. This year sees an all-female list of nominees. They are Ashaine White, Luz, Matilda Mann, Naomi Kimpenu, and PinkPantheress - with each receiving mentorship from a well-established Academy member, as well as support from leaders from Apple Music. Illustrating the true impact of the award, 2021 nominee Holly Humberstone is now in the running for Best Song Musically and Lyrically this year.

Nominations for **PRS for Music Most Performed Work** celebrate the songwriters of five massive hits released in 2021. Leading the category is Songwriter of the Year nominee Ed Sheeran’s ‘Bad Habits’ and ‘Shivers’. Also nominated is ‘Bed’, performed by David Guetta, Joel Corry and Raye, alongside Tom Grennan’s ‘Little Bit of Love’, and Elton John and Dua Lipa’s ‘Cold Heart (PNAU Remix)’.
Recognised for outstanding original music for feature films, nominees for **Best Original Film Score** include Steven Price for the music in Edgar Wright’s psychological thriller ‘Last Night in Soho’ and Jonny Greenwood for the Oscar nominated ‘Spencer’. Also nominated are Chris Roe for ‘After Love’, Emilie Levienaise-Farrouch for her work on ‘Censor’ and Daniel Blumberg for the star-studded and critically acclaimed drama ‘The World to Come’.
The **Best Television Soundtrack** category features five uniquely dramatic, thrilling and insightful productions, with nominations going to Jessica Dannheisser for Second World War documentary ‘Blitz Spirit with Lucy Worsley’, Arthur Sharpe for crime drama ‘Landscapers’ and Stew Jackson and Dan Jones for Stephen Merchant’s comedy ‘The Outlaws’ starring the legendary Christopher Walken. Also nominated for their outstanding original music are Ben Please and Beth Porter for the Oscar nominated Netflix short ‘Robin Robin’, as well as Dominik Scherrer for the Golden Globe nominated BBC thriller ‘The Serpent’.
Nominees for **Best Original Video Game Score** include Richard Jacques for the popular ‘Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy’, Bobby Krlic for third-person shooter game ‘Returnal’ and Benedict Nichols’ score for the beautifully designed ‘Omno’.
All winners will receive a dedicated Ivor Novello Award and join a roll call of songwriting and composing greats that includes Cathy Dennis, Stormzy, Annie Lennox, Paul McCartney, John Lennon, Kate Bush, David Arnold, George Fenton and Joan Armatrading.

**The Ivor Novello Awards**, named after the Welsh entertainer Ivor Novello, are awards for songwriting and composing. They have been presented annually in London by the Ivors Academy, formerly called the British Academy of Songwriters, Composers, and Authors, since 1956.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-about-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-BBC-2)
The awards are presented at two annual ceremonies known as **the Ivors**[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-3) and **the Ivors Composer Awards**.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-4)
*   **The Ivors** take place each May and, as of 2020, are sponsored by Apple Music.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-5) They are recognised worldwide as the major platform for recognising and rewarding Britain and Ireland's songwriting and composing talents.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-BBC-2) The Ivors remain the only award ceremony in the musical calendar that is not influenced by publishers and record companies, but judged and presented by the writing community.

*   **The Ivors Composer Awards** take place each December and are sponsored by PRS for Music.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-6) They are broadcast by BBC Radio 3.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-7)

The award itself is a solid bronze sculpture of Euterpe, the muse of lyric poetry.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-BBC-2) It was designed in 1955 by Hazel Underwood.

### Nominated annual awards
[edit]
*   Best Song Musically and Lyrically  
*   Best Contemporary Song  
*   Album Award  
*   Best Original Film Score  
*   Best Television Soundtrack  
*   Best Original Video Game Score

### Other annual awards

*   Songwriter of the Year  
*   Most Performed Work

*   Jazz Award

*   Outstanding Song Collection  
*   Outstanding Contribution to British Music  
*   Lifetime Achievement

*   BASCA Fellowship  
*   Best Dance Single Award  
*   International Hit of the Year  
*   International Achievement in Musical Theater  
*   Jimmy Kennedy Award  
*   PRS for Music Special International Award  
*   Best Selling UK Single  
*   Best Original Music for a Television/Radio Broadcast  
*   Special Award for Songwriting

### Other annual awards
*   In 1964, John Lennon and Paul McCartney received four nominations for Ivors, including two nominations in the same category (as writers of both of the two songs competing for Highest British Sales of 1963), and were also given a Special Award for Outstanding Services to British Music.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-8)  
*   Lynsey de Paul became the first woman to receive an Ivor Award for "[Won't Somebody Dance with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Won't_Somebody_Dance_with_Me "Won't Somebody Dance with Me")" (The Best Ballad or Romantic Song) in 1974[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-9) and she went on to win another Ivor a year later for her TV theme song "No Honestly".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-10)  
*   In 1976, 10cc musicians Graham Gouldman and Eric Stewart achieved three awards for writing "[I'm Not in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Not_in_Love "I'm Not in Love")" when it won them the Ivors for Most Performed British Work, for Best Pop Song, and for International Hit of the Year.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-11)  
*   In 2008, Amy Winehouse received three nominations for Ivors, including two nominations in the same category (for Best Song Musically & Lyrically).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-13)  
*   In 2010, an Ivor was awarded for the first time to a video game soundtrack, the PS3 title, _Killzone 2_, composed by Joris de Man.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-14)

25 March 2026 - Press release
The Ivors with Amazon Music, 21 May 2026, Grosvenor House London
*   Recognising an outstanding year in British and Irish songwriting, this year’s nominees include globally acclaimed songwriters Olivia Dean, Lola Young, Lily Allen, Wolf Alice, CMAT and Florence + The Machine, alongside a new generation of rising songwriters shaping contemporary music.

*   The Ivor Novello Awards recognise exceptional craft, originality and cultural impact in songwriting and screen composing.

*   Wolf Alice’s Ellie Rowsell, Olivia Dean, Jacob Alon, Self Esteem and co-writer Johan Hugo, and Kae Tempest and co-writer Fraser T Smith all receive two nominations.

*   61 songwriters and composers have been nominated across seven categories celebrating new music released in the UK in 2025.

*   34 receive their first Ivor Novello Award nomination.

*   Nominations recognise songwriting craft across diverse genres including hip-hop / rap, alternative, pop and dance.

*   Listen to The Ivors 2026 playlist on Amazon Music here
Today,The Ivors Academy announces the nominations for the 71st Ivor Novello Awards, with the winners presented at The Ivors with Amazon Music on Thursday 21 May. Peer-judged by songwriters and composers, The Ivors are the most prestigious celebration of the craft, cultural impact and enduring importance of songs and screen compositions. At a time when questions around authorship and AI are reshaping the music landscape, The Ivors stand as a powerful affirmation of human creativity and the cultural value of songwriters.
Recognised as the pinnacle of creative musical achievement since they were first presented in 1956, winning an Ivor Novello is the highest global recognition for songwriting and composing. Winners join a roll call of greats that includes Paul McCartney, John Lennon, George Harrison and Ringo Starr, David Bowie, Adele, RAYE, Stormzy, Bill Withers, Bruce Springsteen, Brian Wilson, Annie Lennox, Amy Winehouse, Dave, Sting, Mick Jagger and Keith Richards, Charli xcx, Lana Del Rey, Lola Young, Lou Reed and Elton John.

Each winner receives an iconic Ivor Novello Award, a solid bronze statuette depicting Euterpe, the Greek muse of music and lyric poetry. The design was created in 1955 by sculptor Hazel Underwood and has remained unchanged ever since.
Tom Gray, Chair of The Ivors Academy, said:“Congratulations to all the songwriters and composers nominated for this year’s Ivor Novello Awards. To be recognised by your peers for exceptional craft and originality at The Ivors is one of the greatest honours in music writing, and we look forward to celebrating their achievements at The Ivors with Amazon Music on 21 May.”
Roberto Neri, Chief Executive of The Ivors Academy, said:“I want to congratulate these incredible nominees, whose work reflects the strength, diversity and global influence of British and Irish songwriting, which we are honoured to celebrate. An Ivor Novello Award has for over 70 years been the most prestigious recognition of excellence in music and I'd like to thank our judges for working hard to recognise this year’s nominees.”
This year, 61 individual British, Irish or UK resident songwriters and composers, and their international collaborators, have received Ivor Novello nominations, with 34 of those picking up a nomination for the first time.
Wolf Alice’s Ellie Rowsell,Olivia Dean, Jacob Alon, Self Esteem and co-writer Johan Hugo, and Kae Tempest and co-writer Fraser T Smith have all received two nominations, with Olivia, Jacob and Johan nominated for the first time by The Ivors Academy.
Little Simz picks up her fifth Ivor Novello nomination, for “Free” in Best Contemporary Song, the second time she has been nominated in this category. She has previously won Best Album in 2020 for Grey Area and Best Contemporary Song in 2022 for“I Love You, I Hate You.”She also received two nominations in the Best Album category in 2022 and 2023.
Lola Young will receive her fourth nomination, with a second for her huge hit “Messy”in the PRS for Music Most Performed Work category.Damon Albarn will receive his fifth nomination with a nod in the Best Contemporary Song category for “Damascus”,having previously won Songwriter of the Year twice and received the Ivor Novello Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016.

Lily Allen receives her third nomination with West End Girl, her first album in seven years, nominated in the Best Album category.Florence Welch receives her fourth nomination at The Ivors, this year in the Best Song Musically and Lyrically category for “Everybody Scream” alongside co-writers Mitski and Mark Bowen.
Coldplay’s huge hit “Vida La Vida” picks up its third nomination this year in the PRS for Music Most Performed Work, off the back of their epic global tour. The song won Best Selling British Single in 2010 and was also nominated for PRS for Music Most Performed Work.
CMAT and Myles Smith both pick up their second Ivor Novello Award nominations, CMAT for her critically acclaimed album EURO-COUNTRY, her second Best Album nomination, and Myles Smith for his worldwide hit, “Stargazing”,alongside co-writers Peter Fenn and Jesse Fink.
The Ivor Novello Award for Best Album celebrates exceptional songwriting craft, creativity and cohesion across the record as a whole. This year’s nominees see a range of spheres of contemporary music represented, including Jim Legxacy’s bold and genre-traversing black british music (2025), Olivia Dean’s divine sophomore The Art Of Loving, Wolf Alice’s sublime fourth album The Clearing, Lily Allen’s punchy and forthright West End Girl, and Irish-star CMAT’s excellent EURO-COUNTRY.
Celebrating innovation and outstanding originality in songwriting,Best Contemporary Song sees nominations for Damon Albarn – “Damascus” (featuring Omar Souleyman and Yasiin Bey), Little Simz – “Free”, Self Esteem – “I Do And I Don’t Care”, and a double nomination for Kae Tempest with both ‘Know Yourself’ and “I Stand On The Line”.
Best Song Musically and Lyrically acknowledges the outstanding craft, quality, coherence and creativity of the songwriting. Nominations this year go to Jacob Alon – “Don’t Fall Asleep”, Florence + The Machine - “Everybody Scream”, Self Esteem - “Focus Is Power”, Wolf Alice - “The Sofa” and Sugababes - “Weeds”.

The PRS for Music Most Performed Work category celebrates songs that received the most broadcast, online and general performances in the last year, based on PRS data. Nominations this year go to Olivia Dean - “Man I Need”, Lola Young - “Messy”, Myles Smith - “Stargazing”, Chrystal - “The Day’s” and Coldplay - “Viva La Vida”.
The Rising Star Award with Amazon Music celebrates British, Irish or UK resident songwriters who are at the tipping point of greatness. This prestigious co-sign this year goes to Chloe Qisha, Divorce, Jacob Alon, kwn, and Skye Newman. Past Rising Star nominees include PinkPantheress, Holly Humberstone and Rachel Chinouriri, with Lola Young winning the award in 2025.
Best Original Film Score recognises outstanding commissioned music that strengthens the storytelling, tone and emotional depth of a feature film. Together, these works amplify the essential role of original composition in elevating the art of film. This year’s nominees consist of Bugonia, composed by Jerskin Fendrix;Dragonfly, composed by Raffertie;Nosferatu, composed by Robin Carolan;Testimony, composed by Tom Hodge; and The Brutalist, composed by Daniel Blumberg.
Best Television Soundtrack celebrates exceptional originally commissioned music that enriches the storytelling and dramatic impact of television programmes in the UK in 2025. This year’s nominees are Adolescence, composed by Aaron May and David Ridley;Lazarus, composed by Sarah Warne;Summerwater, composed by Gazelle Twin;The City Is Ours, composed by Rael Jones; and Trespasses, composed by David Holmes and Brian Irvine. These works highlight the contribution and impact of original music in enhancing storytelling and television viewing.
The award winners will be revealed at The Ivors with Amazon Music on 21 May 2026 at Grosvenor House, London. Alongside these nominations, awards in the Gift of the Academy will be presented to recognise individuals for their lasting contributions to music.

**The Ivor Novello Awards**, named after the Welsh entertainer Ivor Novello, are awards for songwriting and composing. They have been presented annually in London by the Ivors Academy, formerly called the British Academy of Songwriters, Composers, and Authors, since 1956.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-about-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-BBC-2)
The awards are presented at two annual ceremonies known as **the Ivors**[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-3) and **the Ivors Composer Awards**.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-4)
*   **The Ivors** take place each May and, as of 2020, are sponsored by Apple Music.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-5) They are recognised worldwide as the major platform for recognising and rewarding Britain and Ireland's songwriting and composing talents.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-BBC-2) The Ivors remain the only award ceremony in the musical calendar that is not influenced by publishers and record companies, but judged and presented by the writing community.

*   **The Ivors Composer Awards** take place each December and are sponsored by PRS for Music.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-6) They are broadcast by BBC Radio 3.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-7)

*   In 1964, John Lennon and Paul McCartney received four nominations for Ivors, including two nominations in the same category (as writers of both of the two songs competing for Highest British Sales of 1963), and were also given a Special Award for Outstanding Services to British Music.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards#cite_note-8)

This year’s nominees have been revealed, celebrating outstanding songwriters and composers.
We have announced the nominations for The Ivors with Apple Music 2022 for outstanding songwriting and composing across nine categories – including **Songwriter of the Year**, **Best Contemporary Song**, **Best Original Scores for Film, Television and Video Games**, and the **Rising Star Award with Apple Music**.
Recognised as a pinnacle of creative musical achievement since they were first presented in 1956, winning an Ivor Novello Award holds a special place in music as they are judged by award-winning songwriters and composers from The Ivors Academy.
This year’s list of nominations celebrates 77 individual songwriters and composers, including Adele – who is in the running for two awards – and Ed Sheeran, who is nominated for three Ivors. Up for four awards, Dean ‘Inflo’ Josiah Cover is this year’s most nominated songwriter. He is recognised for his work with fellow nominees Cleo Soul and Little Simz, who has also received two nominations.
**Shaznay Lewis, Ivor Novello Award winner and judge for The Ivors**, said: _“It’s been a standout year for music and I am full of admiration for the 77 talented songwriters and composers we are celebrating this year. Their work and words touch on a dizzying range of emotions, and I count myself lucky to have heard their stories. As it has every year since 1956, The Ivors celebrates the outstanding creation of music, and I’d like to say a huge congratulations to every nominee.”_
This year sees five huge artists in the running for **Songwriter of the Year**. The prestigious award recognises songwriters or songwriting partnerships for outstanding bodies of songs released in 2021, with Adele, Coldplay, Dave, Ed Sheeran, and Raye up for the award this year. For the second year, members of The Ivors Academy will vote for the winner.
texts.1:
Celebrating albums released in the UK in 2021 that exhibit creative consistency and exceptional songwriting, this year’s nominees for **Best Album** include Laura Mvula’s ‘Pink Noise’ – co-written with Dann Hume, and Sleaford Mods for ‘Spare Ribs’. Receiving three of his four nominations in this category is Dean ‘Inflo’ Josiah Cover for his work with Cleo Sol on both her album ‘Mother’ and SAULT’s ‘NINE’ alongside fellow co-writer Jack Peñate, and with Little Simz for ‘Sometimes I Might Be Introvert’.
Celebrating excellence in the craft of songwriting, this year’s **Best Song Musically and Lyrically** consists of a star-studded line up with nominations for Rag’n’Bone Man’s ‘All You Ever Wanted’, Adele’s emotional hit ‘Easy On Me’, Ella Henderson’s ‘Let’s Go Home Together’, Sam Fender’s ‘Seventeen Going Under’ and Holly Humberstone’s ‘Haunted House’, with their co-writers.
This year’s category for **Best Contemporary Song** also features Rising Star Award nominee PinkPantheress for ‘Just For Me’, as well as a second nominations Little Simz for ‘I Love You, I Hate You’. Also recognised for outstanding originality in songwriting are Russ Millions and Tion Wayne for ‘Body’, James Blake and SZA for ‘Coming Back’, and FKA twigs, Headie One and Fred again.. for ‘Don’t Judge Me’.
Now in its third year, the **Rising Star Award with Apple Music** discovers, supports and accelerates the careers of the most promising young UK or Irish songwriters. This year sees an all-female list of nominees. They are Ashaine White, Luz, Matilda Mann, Naomi Kimpenu, and PinkPantheress - with each receiving mentorship from a well-established Academy member, as well as support from leaders from Apple Music. Illustrating the true impact of the award, 2021 nominee Holly Humberstone is now in the running for Best Song Musically and Lyrically this year.
texts.2:
Nominations for **PRS for Music Most Performed Work** celebrate the songwriters of five massive hits released in 2021. Leading the category is Songwriter of the Year nominee Ed Sheeran’s ‘Bad Habits’ and ‘Shivers’. Also nominated is ‘Bed’, performed by David Guetta, Joel Corry and Raye, alongside Tom Grennan’s ‘Little Bit of Love’, and Elton John and Dua Lipa’s ‘Cold Heart (PNAU Remix)’.
Recognised for outstanding original music for feature films, nominees for **Best Original Film Score** include Steven Price for the music in Edgar Wright’s psychological thriller ‘Last Night in Soho’ and Jonny Greenwood for the Oscar nominated ‘Spencer’. Also nominated are Chris Roe for ‘After Love’, Emilie Levienaise-Farrouch for her work on ‘Censor’ and Daniel Blumberg for the star-studded and critically acclaimed drama ‘The World to Come’.
The **Best Television Soundtrack** category features five uniquely dramatic, thrilling and insightful productions, with nominations going to Jessica Dannheisser for Second World War documentary ‘Blitz Spirit with Lucy Worsley’, Arthur Sharpe for crime drama ‘Landscapers’ and Stew Jackson and Dan Jones for Stephen Merchant’s comedy ‘The Outlaws’ starring the legendary Christopher Walken. Also nominated for their outstanding original music are Ben Please and Beth Porter for the Oscar nominated Netflix short ‘Robin Robin’, as well as Dominik Scherrer for the Golden Globe nominated BBC thriller ‘The Serpent’.
Nominees for **Best Original Video Game Score** include Richard Jacques for the popular ‘Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy’, Bobby Krlic for third-person shooter game ‘Returnal’ and Benedict Nichols’ score for the beautifully designed ‘Omno’.
All winners will receive a dedicated Ivor Novello Award and join a roll call of songwriting and composing greats that includes Cathy Dennis, Stormzy, Annie Lennox, Paul McCartney, John Lennon, Kate Bush, David Arnold, George Fenton and Joan Armatrading.

Question: "The singer that won the lvor Novello Lifetime Achievement award in the same year that the singers of the end credits song for the sitcom that former first child Chelsea Clinton appeared in in 2022 were nominated but did not win, had 3 songs that made it into the UK top 40 official singles. One of these songs was a collaboration with a singer who's song was covered on the sitcom, but which musical was the song originally written for?"

We need:

1. Identify the sitcom that Chelsea Clinton appeared in in 2022. That's Derry Girls (final episode in May 2022). The end credits song for this sitcom: The end credits song is "Dreams" by The Cranberries. (Or the closing theme? Let's check: In Derry Girls, the end credits uses "Dreams" by The Cranberries.)

Thus, the singers of the end credits song: The Cranberries consists of lead vocalist Dolores O'Riordan (female) and bassist Noel Hogan (male). Actually the group has multiple members: Dolores O'Riordan, Noel Hogan, Mike Hogan, Fergal Lawler. The main singers are Dolores O'Riordan (lead singer) and Noel Hogan (guitarist) may not sing lead. But the end credits song is performed by The Cranberries as a group. So the singers of that song would include Dolores O'Riordan and Noel Hogan? Actually Noel Hogan is a guitarist, not a singer, but he might provide backing vocals. However "Dreams" is performed by the band. We'll assume the singer(s) = Dolores O'Riordan (lead vocalist) and Noel Hogan (guitarist). But the question: "the singers of the end credits song for the sitcom... were nominated but did not win." Which nomination? Likely refers to Ivor Novello nominations the same year as the Lifetime Achievement award winner. So the singers were nominated for an Ivor Novello award but did not win that year.

Which year? We need the year the Ivor Novello Lifetime Achievement award was given to a singer, and that same year the singers of "Dreams" were nominated but did not win. Which year's ceremony had the Lifetime Achievement award? Let's look at the Ivor Novello winners.

Title: Nominations announced for The Ivors 2022
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
This year’s nominees have been revealed, celebrating outstanding songwriters and composers.
We have announced the nominations for The Ivors with Apple Music 2022 for outstanding songwriting and composing across nine categories – including **Songwriter of the Year**, **Best Contemporary Song**, **Best Original Scores for Film, Television and Video Games**, and the **Rising Star Award with Apple Music**.
Recognised as a pinnacle of creative musical achievement since they were first presented in 1956, winning an Ivor Novello Award holds a special place in music as they are judged by award-winning songwriters and composers from The Ivors Academy.
This year’s list of nominations celebrates 77 individual songwriters and composers, including Adele – who is in the running for two awards – and Ed Sheeran, who is nominated for three Ivors. Up for four awards, Dean ‘Inflo’ Josiah Cover is this year’s most nominated songwriter. He is recognised for his work with fellow nominees Cleo Soul and Little Simz, who has also received two nominations.
**Shaznay Lewis, Ivor Novello Award winner and judge for The Ivors**, said: _“It’s been a standout year for music and I am full of admiration for the 77 talented songwriters and composers we are celebrating this year. Their work and words touch on a dizzying range of emotions, and I count myself lucky to have heard their stories. As it has every year since 1956, The Ivors celebrates the outstanding creation of music, and I’d like to say a huge congratulations to every nominee.”_
This year sees five huge artists in the running for **Songwriter of the Year**. The prestigious award recognises songwriters or songwriting partnerships for outstanding bodies of songs released in 2021, with Adele, Coldplay, Dave, Ed Sheeran, and Raye up for the award this year. For the second year, members of The Ivors Academy will vote for the winner.

Celebrating albums released in the UK in 2021 that exhibit creative consistency and exceptional songwriting, this year’s nominees for **Best Album** include Laura Mvula’s ‘Pink Noise’ – co-written with Dann Hume, and Sleaford Mods for ‘Spare Ribs’. Receiving three of his four nominations in this category is Dean ‘Inflo’ Josiah Cover for his work with Cleo Sol on both her album ‘Mother’ and SAULT’s ‘NINE’ alongside fellow co-writer Jack Peñate, and with Little Simz for ‘Sometimes I Might Be Introvert’.
Celebrating excellence in the craft of songwriting, this year’s **Best Song Musically and Lyrically** consists of a star-studded line up with nominations for Rag’n’Bone Man’s ‘All You Ever Wanted’, Adele’s emotional hit ‘Easy On Me’, Ella Henderson’s ‘Let’s Go Home Together’, Sam Fender’s ‘Seventeen Going Under’ and Holly Humberstone’s ‘Haunted House’, with their co-writers.
This year’s category for **Best Contemporary Song** also features Rising Star Award nominee PinkPantheress for ‘Just For Me’, as well as a second nominations Little Simz for ‘I Love You, I Hate You’. Also recognised for outstanding originality in songwriting are Russ Millions and Tion Wayne for ‘Body’, James Blake and SZA for ‘Coming Back’, and FKA twigs, Headie One and Fred again.. for ‘Don’t Judge Me’.
Now in its third year, the **Rising Star Award with Apple Music** discovers, supports and accelerates the careers of the most promising young UK or Irish songwriters. This year sees an all-female list of nominees. They are Ashaine White, Luz, Matilda Mann, Naomi Kimpenu, and PinkPantheress - with each receiving mentorship from a well-established Academy member, as well as support from leaders from Apple Music. Illustrating the true impact of the award, 2021 nominee Holly Humberstone is now in the running for Best Song Musically and Lyrically this year.

Nominations for **PRS for Music Most Performed Work** celebrate the songwriters of five massive hits released in 2021. Leading the category is Songwriter of the Year nominee Ed Sheeran’s ‘Bad Habits’ and ‘Shivers’. Also nominated is ‘Bed’, performed by David Guetta, Joel Corry and Raye, alongside Tom Grennan’s ‘Little Bit of Love’, and Elton John and Dua Lipa’s ‘Cold Heart (PNAU Remix)’.
Recognised for outstanding original music for feature films, nominees for **Best Original Film Score** include Steven Price for the music in Edgar Wright’s psychological thriller ‘Last Night in Soho’ and Jonny Greenwood for the Oscar nominated ‘Spencer’. Also nominated are Chris Roe for ‘After Love’, Emilie Levienaise-Farrouch for her work on ‘Censor’ and Daniel Blumberg for the star-studded and critically acclaimed drama ‘The World to Come’.
The **Best Television Soundtrack** category features five uniquely dramatic, thrilling and insightful productions, with nominations going to Jessica Dannheisser for Second World War documentary ‘Blitz Spirit with Lucy Worsley’, Arthur Sharpe for crime drama ‘Landscapers’ and Stew Jackson and Dan Jones for Stephen Merchant’s comedy ‘The Outlaws’ starring the legendary Christopher Walken. Also nominated for their outstanding original music are Ben Please and Beth Porter for the Oscar nominated Netflix short ‘Robin Robin’, as well as Dominik Scherrer for the Golden Globe nominated BBC thriller ‘The Serpent’.
Nominees for **Best Original Video Game Score** include Richard Jacques for the popular ‘Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy’, Bobby Krlic for third-person shooter game ‘Returnal’ and Benedict Nichols’ score for the beautifully designed ‘Omno’.
All winners will receive a dedicated Ivor Novello Award and join a roll call of songwriting and composing greats that includes Cathy Dennis, Stormzy, Annie Lennox, Paul McCartney, John Lennon, Kate Bush, David Arnold, George Fenton and Joan Armatrading.

The Ivors Academy have today announced the nominations for the 71 st Ivor Novello Awards, with the winners presented at The Ivors with Amazon Music on Thursday 21 May.
Peer-judged by songwriters and composers, The Ivors are the most prestigious celebration of the craft, cultural impact and enduring importance of songs and screen compositions.
At a time when questions around authorship and AI are reshaping the music landscape, The Ivors stand as a powerful affirmation of human creativity and the cultural value of songwriters.
This year, 61 individual British, Irish or UK resident songwriters and composers, and their international collaborators, have received Ivor Novello nominations, with 34 of those picking up a nomination for the first time.
Wolf Alice’s**Ellie Rowsell**,**Olivia Dean, Jacob Alon, Self Esteem**and co-writer**Johan Hugo**, and**Kae Tempest**and co-writer**Fraser T Smith**have all received two nominations, with Olivia, Jacob and Johan nominated for the first time by The Ivors Academy.
**Little Simz**picks up her fifth Ivor Novello nomination, for “Free” in Best Contemporary Song, the second time she has been nominated in this category. She has previously won Best Album in 2020 for _Grey Area_ and Best Contemporary Song in 2022 for“I Love You, I Hate You _.”_ She also received two nominations in the Best Album category in 2022 and 2023.
**Lola Young**will receive her fourth nomination, with a second for her huge hit “Messy”in the PRS for Music Most Performed Work category.**Damon Albarn**will receive his fifth nomination with a nod in the Best Contemporary Song category for “Damascus”_,_ having previously won Songwriter of the Year twice and received the Ivor Novello Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016.
**Lily Allen**receives her third nomination with _West End Girl_, her first album in seven years, nominated in the Best Album category.**Florence Welch**receives her fourth nomination at The Ivors, this year in the Best Song Musically and Lyrically category for “Everybody Scream” alongside co-writers**Mitski**and**Mark Bowen**.

**Coldplay’s**huge hit “Vida La Vida” picks up its third nomination this year in the PRS for Music Most Performed Work, off the back of their epic global tour. The song won Best Selling British Single in 2010 and was also nominated for PRS for Music Most Performed Work.
**CMAT**and**Myles Smith**both pick up their second Ivor Novello Award nominations, CMAT for her critically acclaimed album _EURO-COUNTRY_, her second Best Album nomination, and Myles Smith for his worldwide hit, “Stargazing”_,_ alongside co-writers Peter Fenn and Jesse Fink.

This year’s nominees have been revealed, celebrating outstanding songwriters and composers.
We have announced the nominations for The Ivors with Apple Music 2022 for outstanding songwriting and composing across nine categories – including **Songwriter of the Year**, **Best Contemporary Song**, **Best Original Scores for Film, Television and Video Games**, and the **Rising Star Award with Apple Music**.
Recognised as a pinnacle of creative musical achievement since they were first presented in 1956, winning an Ivor Novello Award holds a special place in music as they are judged by award-winning songwriters and composers from The Ivors Academy.
This year’s list of nominations celebrates 77 individual songwriters and composers, including Adele – who is in the running for two awards – and Ed Sheeran, who is nominated for three Ivors. Up for four awards, Dean ‘Inflo’ Josiah Cover is this year’s most nominated songwriter. He is recognised for his work with fellow nominees Cleo Soul and Little Simz, who has also received two nominations.
**Shaznay Lewis, Ivor Novello Award winner and judge for The Ivors**, said: _“It’s been a standout year for music and I am full of admiration for the 77 talented songwriters and composers we are celebrating this year. Their work and words touch on a dizzying range of emotions, and I count myself lucky to have heard their stories. As it has every year since 1956, The Ivors celebrates the outstanding creation of music, and I’d like to say a huge congratulations to every nominee.”_
This year sees five huge artists in the running for **Songwriter of the Year**. The prestigious award recognises songwriters or songwriting partnerships for outstanding bodies of songs released in 2021, with Adele, Coldplay, Dave, Ed Sheeran, and Raye up for the award this year. For the second year, members of The Ivors Academy will vote for the winner.
texts.1:
Celebrating albums released in the UK in 2021 that exhibit creative consistency and exceptional songwriting, this year’s nominees for **Best Album** include Laura Mvula’s ‘Pink Noise’ – co-written with Dann Hume, and Sleaford Mods for ‘Spare Ribs’. Receiving three of his four nominations in this category is Dean ‘Inflo’ Josiah Cover for his work with Cleo Sol on both her album ‘Mother’ and SAULT’s ‘NINE’ alongside fellow co-writer Jack Peñate, and with Little Simz for ‘Sometimes I Might Be Introvert’.
Celebrating excellence in the craft of songwriting, this year’s **Best Song Musically and Lyrically** consists of a star-studded line up with nominations for Rag’n’Bone Man’s ‘All You Ever Wanted’, Adele’s emotional hit ‘Easy On Me’, Ella Henderson’s ‘Let’s Go Home Together’, Sam Fender’s ‘Seventeen Going Under’ and Holly Humberstone’s ‘Haunted House’, with their co-writers.
This year’s category for **Best Contemporary Song** also features Rising Star Award nominee PinkPantheress for ‘Just For Me’, as well as a second nominations Little Simz for ‘I Love You, I Hate You’. Also recognised for outstanding originality in songwriting are Russ Millions and Tion Wayne for ‘Body’, James Blake and SZA for ‘Coming Back’, and FKA twigs, Headie One and Fred again.. for ‘Don’t Judge Me’.
Now in its third year, the **Rising Star Award with Apple Music** discovers, supports and accelerates the careers of the most promising young UK or Irish songwriters. This year sees an all-female list of nominees. They are Ashaine White, Luz, Matilda Mann, Naomi Kimpenu, and PinkPantheress - with each receiving mentorship from a well-established Academy member, as well as support from leaders from Apple Music. Illustrating the true impact of the award, 2021 nominee Holly Humberstone is now in the running for Best Song Musically and Lyrically this year.
texts.2:
Nominations for **PRS for Music Most Performed Work** celebrate the songwriters of five massive hits released in 2021. Leading the category is Songwriter of the Year nominee Ed Sheeran’s ‘Bad Habits’ and ‘Shivers’. Also nominated is ‘Bed’, performed by David Guetta, Joel Corry and Raye, alongside Tom Grennan’s ‘Little Bit of Love’, and Elton John and Dua Lipa’s ‘Cold Heart (PNAU Remix)’.
Recognised for outstanding original music for feature films, nominees for **Best Original Film Score** include Steven Price for the music in Edgar Wright’s psychological thriller ‘Last Night in Soho’ and Jonny Greenwood for the Oscar nominated ‘Spencer’. Also nominated are Chris Roe for ‘After Love’, Emilie Levienaise-Farrouch for her work on ‘Censor’ and Daniel Blumberg for the star-studded and critically acclaimed drama ‘The World to Come’.
The **Best Television Soundtrack** category features five uniquely dramatic, thrilling and insightful productions, with nominations going to Jessica Dannheisser for Second World War documentary ‘Blitz Spirit with Lucy Worsley’, Arthur Sharpe for crime drama ‘Landscapers’ and Stew Jackson and Dan Jones for Stephen Merchant’s comedy ‘The Outlaws’ starring the legendary Christopher Walken. Also nominated for their outstanding original music are Ben Please and Beth Porter for the Oscar nominated Netflix short ‘Robin Robin’, as well as Dominik Scherrer for the Golden Globe nominated BBC thriller ‘The Serpent’.
Nominees for **Best Original Video Game Score** include Richard Jacques for the popular ‘Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy’, Bobby Krlic for third-person shooter game ‘Returnal’ and Benedict Nichols’ score for the beautifully designed ‘Omno’.
All winners will receive a dedicated Ivor Novello Award and join a roll call of songwriting and composing greats that includes Cathy Dennis, Stormzy, Annie Lennox, Paul McCartney, John Lennon, Kate Bush, David Arnold, George Fenton and Joan Armatrading.

The Ivors Academy have today announced the nominations for the 71 st Ivor Novello Awards, with the winners presented at The Ivors with Amazon Music on Thursday 21 May.
Peer-judged by songwriters and composers, The Ivors are the most prestigious celebration of the craft, cultural impact and enduring importance of songs and screen compositions.
At a time when questions around authorship and AI are reshaping the music landscape, The Ivors stand as a powerful affirmation of human creativity and the cultural value of songwriters.
This year, 61 individual British, Irish or UK resident songwriters and composers, and their international collaborators, have received Ivor Novello nominations, with 34 of those picking up a nomination for the first time.
Wolf Alice’s**Ellie Rowsell**,**Olivia Dean, Jacob Alon, Self Esteem**and co-writer**Johan Hugo**, and**Kae Tempest**and co-writer**Fraser T Smith**have all received two nominations, with Olivia, Jacob and Johan nominated for the first time by The Ivors Academy.
**Little Simz**picks up her fifth Ivor Novello nomination, for “Free” in Best Contemporary Song, the second time she has been nominated in this category. She has previously won Best Album in 2020 for _Grey Area_ and Best Contemporary Song in 2022 for“I Love You, I Hate You _.”_ She also received two nominations in the Best Album category in 2022 and 2023.
**Lola Young**will receive her fourth nomination, with a second for her huge hit “Messy”in the PRS for Music Most Performed Work category.**Damon Albarn**will receive his fifth nomination with a nod in the Best Contemporary Song category for “Damascus”_,_ having previously won Songwriter of the Year twice and received the Ivor Novello Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016.
**Lily Allen**receives her third nomination with _West End Girl_, her first album in seven years, nominated in the Best Album category.**Florence Welch**receives her fourth nomination at The Ivors, this year in the Best Song Musically and Lyrically category for “Everybody Scream” alongside co-writers**Mitski**and**Mark Bowen**.

Also nominated: _Wannabe_, performed by**Spice Girls**,written by **Victoria Adams**, **Melanie Brown**, **Emma Bunton**, **Melanie Chisholm**, **Geri Halliwell**, **Matt Rowe** and **Richard Stannard**

*   Outstanding Song Collection: **Richard Thompson**  
*   Best Song Musically and Lyrically: _Too Much Love Will Kill You_, performed by**Queen**,written by **Brian May**, **Frank Musker** and **Elizabeth Lamers**. Also nominated: _I Am I Feel_, performed by**Alisha’s Attic**,written by **Terence Martin**, **Karen Poole** and **Michelle Poole**;_Neighbourhood_, performed by**Space**,written by **Thomas Scott**, **Andrew Parle**, **James Edwards** and **Francis Griffiths**

*   International Hit of the Year: _Wannabe_

The 1998 Ivor Novello ceremony took place on 28th May 1998 at Grosvenor House, London.

We need to find year when that singer(s) nominated but no win. Which award? Possibly a music award? Wait: question wording: "The singer that won the lvor Novello Lifetime Achievement award in the same year that the singers of the end credits song for the sitcom that former first child Chelsea Clinton appeared in in 2022 were nominated but did not win". So we want singer who won the Ivor Novello Lifetime Achievement award in year X. So we need to identify year X where The Cranberries were nominated but didn't win. Could be for Ivor Novello? Check 2022 nominees: The Cranberries maybe nominated, but did not win. 2022 Ivor Novello nominations included maybe The Cranberries? Not sure. The 2022 nominations list earlier: various nominees, but I didn't see The Cranberries. Actually 2022 nomination list earlier in results didn't mention Cranberries.

News
April 7, 2022  
Nominees for the 2022 Ivor Novello Awards have been announced, with several Sony Music artists in the running for the prestigious songwriting accolades.
Adele received two nominations: Best Song Musically and Lyrically for ‘Easy On Me’ and Songwriter of the Year.
Rag’n’Bone Man is also in the running for Best Song Musically and Lyrically, for ‘All You Ever Wanted’ from the No.1 album _Life By Misadventure_.
In the PRS For Music Most Performed Work category, Tom Grennan is shortlisted for the single ‘Little Bit of Love’ from his chart-topping _Evering Road_ LP.
Sony Masterworks composer Bobby Krlic also received a nomination, with _Returnal_ up for Best Original Video Game Score.
This year’s ceremony will be the 67th Ivors presentation, taking place in London on 19 th May. Check out the full list of nominees atIvorsAcademy.com.
